correctness.rationale: Conditioning on whether the points fall on one circle gives uniform [0,h/2] distances; crossing circles adds independent vertex-distance uniforms. Independently expanded the exact general moment sum using symbolic algebra and confirmed μ=(L-c)/4, ν=(L-c)^2/12, ω=((L-c)^3+c^3)/32 with c=ab/L, whence Δ=ω-2μ³=c³/32. Solving L=4μ+c and quadratic z²-Lz+Lc yields complete positive-real feasibility μ>0,ν=4μ²/3,2μ³<ω<=56μ³/27, and unique unordered lengths. First two coincide with a circle of length 4μ. The cube-root Hölder estimate follows from concavity; c=ε,2ε at fixed μ proves exponent 1/3 sharp even with positive circles. Inspected independent code verify_figure8.py and its exact conditional integrals; numerical tests supplement general algebra.

value.rationale: Recovering a metric-graph topology parameter from unlabeled random pair-distance moments is an intrinsic inverse problem. The exact point at which a pair of circles ceases to mimic a single circle, the complete realizable surface and optimal inverse stability give natural and potentially reusable benchmark facts, despite simple final algebra after prior forward-moment methods.

limitations: Inverse classification assumes exactly two positive circles glued at one point; no identification claim for arbitrary metric graphs or noisy finite samples.
Sharp inverse modulus applies to c and L, not necessarily individually ordered lengths at equal-circle discriminant.
